# Pedestrian Safety Research Group, Tsinghua University

> Research group led by Bingbing Nie at the School of Vehicle and Mobility and the State Key Laboratory of Intelligent Green Vehicle and Mobility, Tsinghua University, Beijing. We study pedestrian and vulnerable-road-user safety as one loop: measure real human reactions in safety-critical scenarios, build road-user models with realistic dynamic behaviors, and design AI-driven integrated safety systems that reduce injury.

Contact: nbb@tsinghua.edu.cn. PI ORCID: 0000-0002-8529-8613.

## Research directions

1. Pedestrian behavior and pedestrian–vehicle interaction. Immersive VR conflicts with motion capture and EEG quantify the perception–decision–execution timeline, a distance-based safety envelope, urgency-dependent decision uncertainty, and three decision modes (no-risk, game, life-saving). Extends to e-scooter riders and cyclists.
2. Road user modeling with realistic dynamic behaviors. Digital pedestrians with risk perception, avoidance decision and kinematic response (CARLA); RLHF-fine-tuned trajectory prediction for rare avoidance behaviors; age-scaling of avoidance kinematics.
3. AI-driven integrated safety and injury prevention (risk-to-injury). Activation strategies for AEB/AES/deployable devices from reconstructed crashes; prediction-based active-hood triggering ~200 ms before impact; risk perception learned from safety-driver takeovers in an L3 autonomous fleet.

- Nie B et al. Safety envelope of pedestrians upon motor vehicle conflicts identified via active avoidance behaviour. Sci Rep 2021;11:3996. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-021-82331-z
- Li Q et al. Pedestrian decision-making uncertainty in urgent scenarios modulates multi-level, neural hierarchies. Cell Rep Phys Sci 2025;6:102401. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.xcrp.2024.102401
- Liu S et al. How pedestrians react to imminent vehicle threats: a virtual reality study in safety-critical scenarios. Accid Anal Prev 2026;236:108690. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.aap.2026.108690
- Huang Y et al. Are riders of electric two-wheelers safer than bicyclists in collisions with motor vehicles? Accid Anal Prev 2020;134:105336. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.aap.2019.105336
- Liu S et al. Pedestrian trajectory prediction with reinforcement learning from a human-designed reward model. IEEE Intell Transp Syst Mag 2026. https://doi.org/10.1109/MITS.2026.3661479
- Gao X et al. Pedestrian modeling with realistic dynamic behaviors and its application in virtual safety testing for autonomous vehicles. Accid Anal Prev 2026;225:108328. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.aap.2025.108328
- Liu S et al. Investigation of pre-crash avoidance kinematics in pedestrians of different ages through volunteer experiment and scaling methodology. Traffic Inj Prev 2025;26:281–290. https://doi.org/10.1080/15389588.2024.2408402
- Li Q et al. Activation strategies and effectiveness of intelligent safety systems for reducing pedestrian injuries in autonomous vehicles. Accid Anal Prev 2025;211:107870. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.aap.2024.107870
- Sun H et al. A prediction-based framework for developing integrated pedestrian safety systems under high-risk scenarios. Accid Anal Prev 2026;233:108560. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.aap.2026.108560
- Luo Y et al. Modeling pedestrian-vehicle interaction risk based on risk perception of experienced drivers in autonomous vehicles. Traffic Inj Prev 2026. https://doi.org/10.1080/15389588.2026.2697052

## Data and code

- P-RLHF safety-critical pedestrian trajectory dataset (1,920 VR interaction segments): https://github.com/siyuanl5-jpg/P-RLHF
- Decision-uncertainty analysis code: https://zenodo.org/records/14257262
